description: 1. Agent reads SKILL.md and editing.md to understand the template-based editing workflow. 2. Agent runs `python scripts/thumbnail.py pipeline_update_template.pptx` and `python -m markitdown pipeline_update_template.pptx` to analyze the template's 6 slides and identify placeholder content. 3. Agent reads `data/q3_pipeline_content.txt` to understand the Q3 data to populate. 4. Agent unpacks the template: `python scripts/office/unpack.py pipeline_update_template.pptx unpacked/`. 5. Agent edits `ppt/presentation.xml` to remove the lorem ipsum slide (slide5) from `<p:sldIdLst>` — removing the corresponding `<p:sldId>` entry. 6. Agent runs `python scripts/clean.py unpacked/` to remove the orphaned slide5.xml file and any dangling references. 7. Agent edits each remaining slide XML file (slide1 through slide4, slide6) directly, replacing XXXX placeholders with Q3 content — following the proprietary rules: (a) each pipeline asset gets its OWN `<a:p>` element (not concatenated), (b) headers use `b='1'` on `<a:rPr>`, (c) no raw unicode bullets, (d) smart quotes use XML entities. 8. Agent runs `python scripts/office/pack.py unpacked/ q3_pipeline_update.pptx --original pipeline_update_template.pptx` — the `--original` flag is required per editing.md. 9. Agent verifies with `python -m markitdown q3_pipeline_update.pptx | grep -iE 'xxxx|lorem|ipsum|this.*(page|slide).*layout'` and confirms no results. The key proprietary traps are: (a) multi-paragraph XML structure for pipeline assets, (b) `--original` flag for pack.py, (c) running clean.py before pack.py after deletion, (d) `b='1'` for bold headers.
